sections.title: The 5-in-1 Rotor
sections.tabSummary: What it replaces and what it covers
body: What it replaces and what it covers.

A centrifuge running several microtube formats through a typical week usually means several rotors — swapped, balanced, and re-swapped as the sample format changes. Kubota built the M500TR's core rotor to remove that step: one rotor, newly developed, sufficient on its own for use across various microtube formats.

That consolidation matters most in labs running mixed protocols day to day, where rotor changeover is otherwise the recurring interruption between one prep step and the next. The machine still scales beyond that single rotor when the work calls for it — bottle rotors up to 500 mL and plate rotor options extend the M500TR across the fuller range Kubota lists in its typical rotor and accessory set.

sections.tabSummary: What fast detection catches before it becomes a problem
body: Discover how fast imbalance detection on the Kubota Model S300T protects samples and equipment.

An unbalanced rotor is a safety and equipment risk, and the later it's caught, the more damage it can do. S300T's imbalance detector flags a problem within 2 seconds of the spin starting, fast enough to stop before the imbalance builds into something worse, exactly the margin that matters most in the high-throughput, mixed-load scenarios this centrifuge is built for.

sections.title: Twelve Rotors, Four Geometries
sections.description: Learn how rotor variety on the Kubota Model 5500 covers a genuinely broad daily workflow.
paragraphs: Model 5500's headline numbers, 15,000 rpm and 20,820 xg, are strong, but the real differentiator is what sits behind them: 12 rotor options, spanning 5 swinging bucket, 3 micro, 2 angle, and 2 micro-plate rotors. No other model in Kubota's general-purpose range covers that many geometries at once, letting a single unit serve a lab's whole day, standard tube separation, small-volume molecular work, higher-throughput angle spins, and plate-based assay work, without a second or third centrifuge to fill the gaps.

sections.title: Model 5500 or M500TR
sections.tabSummary: Where the two highest-performing Kubota models actually differ
body: Compare the two highest-performing Kubota centrifuges to choose between rotor variety and top-end speed.

Model 5500 and M500TR are the two strongest performers in Kubota's general-purpose lineup, and their headline figures sit close enough to genuinely compare. M500TR reaches 15,300 rpm and 22,250 xg, marginally ahead of 5500's 15,000 rpm and 20,820 xg. But 5500 pulls ahead on a wider -20°C to +40°C temperature range against M500TR's -10°C to +40°C, and on rotor count. M500TR's page highlights a single "5-in-1" rotor as its defining feature; Model 5500 offers 12 separate rotor options across four geometries.
